verses.1: He shows mercy who lends to his neighbor, for he keeps the commandments by strengthening him.
verses.2: Lend to your neighbor in his time of need, and receive it again from your neighbor in his time.
verses.3: Keep your word, and act faithfully with him, and then you will find whatever you need in every time.
verses.4: Many have treated a loan like found money, and they offered trouble to those who helped them.
verses.5: Until they receive, they kiss the hands of the giver, and they humble their voice in promises.
verses.6: But at the time of repayment, they will ask for more time, and they will speak annoying and complaining words, and they will make excuses for the time.
verses.7: Then, if he is able to repay, he will turn away. He will pay barely one half, and he will consider it as if he had found it.
verses.8: But if not, then he will defraud him of his money, and he will have him as an enemy without cause.
verses.9: And he will repay him with accusations and curses, and he will repay him with contempt, instead of with honor and kindness.
verses.10: Many have refused to lend, not because of wickedness, but because they were afraid to be defrauded without cause.
verses.11: Yet truly, be more steadfast toward the humble, and you should not delay in acts of mercy toward them.
verses.12: Assist the poor because of the commandment. And you should not send him away empty because of his dire need.
verses.13: Lose your money to your brother and your friend. For you should not hide it under a stone to be lost.
verses.14: Let your treasure be in the precepts of the Most High, and it will benefit you more than gold.
verses.15: Store your alms in the hearts of the poor, and it will obtain help for you against all evil.
verses.16: Better than the shield or the lance of a powerful man,
verses.17: it will fight for you against your enemy.
verses.18: A good man offers credit for the sake of his neighbor. But one who abandons him to himself will perish in shame.
verses.19: You should not forget the kindness of your benefactor. For he has offered his life on your behalf.
verses.20: The sinner and the unclean flee from such promises.
verses.21: A sinner attributes to himself the goods of his loan. And an ungrateful mind will abandon the one who has freed him.
verses.22: A man offers credit to his neighbor. But when he will have lost respect, he will abandon him.
verses.23: A wicked promise has destroyed many who had good intentions, and has tossed them like a wave on the ocean.
verses.24: It has caused powerful men to travel around, and they have wandered amid foreign nations.
verses.25: A sinner transgressing the commandment of the Lord will fall into a wicked promise. And he who undertakes many things will fall into judgment.
verses.26: Help your neighbor to recover according to your ability, but attend to yourself, lest you also fall.
verses.27: The primary need in a man’s life is water and bread, and clothing, and a house to protect modesty.
verses.28: A pauper’s food under a roof of boards is better than a splendid feast on a sojourn away from home.
verses.29: Let yourself be pleased with little instead of much, and you will not hear the reproach of being away from home.
verses.30: It is a wicked life to go from house to house as a guest. For wherever he is a guest, he will not act confidently, nor open his mouth.
verses.31: He will entertain, and feed, and give drink to the ungrateful, and beyond this, he will listen to bitter words:
verses.32: “Go, my guest, and set the table, and let others eat from what you have in your hand.”
verses.33: “Depart from the honored face of my friends. For it has become necessary for my house to host my brother instead.”
verses.34: These things are grievous to a man having understanding: to take advantage of a household, and to reproach a lender. [ Sirach 30 ]
